claim: ADO-001's validation_surfaces and section 3 both name a TFVC negative fixture that does not exist anywhere under Plans/. This re-commits the exact defect AZ-01 was raised to repair and breaches atom-azure-az-01's negative constraint against naming a fixture surface that is not written.
evidence: ADO-001 validation_surfaces reads '[Plans/azure_devops_integration_fixtures.json, missing-project and variant negative tests, null-project and TFVC negative fixtures]'. Section 3 reads 'validates Services and Server adapter profiles, a missing-project negative, a null-project negative and a TFVC-container negative'. Plans/azure_devops_integration_fixtures.json invalid[] holds exactly five entries: azure_devops_repository_cannot_drop_project_identity, azure_devops_repository_cannot_null_the_project, azure_devops_repository_cannot_omit_the_project_guid, azure_devops_project_guid_cannot_be_a_display_name, azure_devops_profile_cannot_declare_a_read_side_policy_scope_failure. grep -ri tfvc over Plans/*.json returns the token tfvc_container_unsupported only twice, both as members of unsupported_reason_codes inside the two positive adapter profiles; no fixture exercises TFVC container recognition, and no fixture name contains tfvc.
suggested_repair: Either write the TFVC-container negative fixture, or drop 'TFVC' from ADO-001's validation_surfaces and from section 3 and state that TFVC recognition is stated and not yet falsifiable by a fixture, exactly as ADO-003 does for the review fixtures.

claim: ADO-005's new validation_surfaces prose asserts the Azure fixture pack holds the two adapter profiles and the repository-binding negatives 'and nothing else', an exhaustiveness claim the same commit range falsifies by adding a provider_instance_profile positive and a provider_adapter_profile negative to that pack.
evidence: ADO-005 validation_surfaces: 'That pack holds the Services and Server adapter profiles and the repository-binding negatives and nothing else.' Plans/azure_devops_integration_fixtures.json valid[] now holds three entries, the third being azure_devops_server_instance_profile (definition provider_instance_profile, added by AZ-23), and invalid[] holds azure_devops_profile_cannot_declare_a_read_side_policy_scope_failure, whose definition is provider_adapter_profile, not repository_binding.
suggested_repair: Replace 'and nothing else' with the pack's actual contents: the two adapter profiles, the Azure DevOps Server instance profile, the repository-binding negatives and the profile reason-code negative.

claim: The ledger's finding record for AZ-17 states that 'both policy conditionals require them', meaning policy_scope_ref and expected_policy_set. Only one of the two policy conditionals requires policy_scope_ref.
evidence: Plans/forge_integration_contracts.schema.json $defs/command_request/allOf[19] (if command_id const cmd.forge.repository.policy.preview) has then.properties.target.required = ['policy_resource_id','policy_scope_ref','provider_patch_ref','expected_policy_revision','expected_policy_set']. allOf[20] (if command_id const cmd.forge.repository.policy.apply) has then.properties.target.required = ['policy_preview_ref','expected_policy_revision','expected_policy_set'] and names policy_scope_ref nowhere; target.properties for that branch are only expected_policy_revision, expected_policy_set, policy_preview_ref. Enumerating every branch that names policy_scope_ref gives five loci, none of them under allOf[20].
suggested_repair: Either reword the AZ-17 record to say the preview conditional requires both and the apply conditional inherits the scope through policy_preview_ref, or add policy_scope_ref to allOf[20]'s required list.

claim: AZ-19's rule that an absent canonical URL must state why is unevadable in the source-control carrier but evadable by omission in the forge gate_record, where canonical_url, canonical_url_origin and url_absent_reason are all optional. A gate_record that simply omits the three validates and says nothing about the missing URL.
evidence: Plans/source_control_contracts.schema.json $defs/normalized_remote_record puts canonical_url, canonical_url_origin and url_absent_reason all in required, so its two url conditionals always fire. Plans/forge_integration_contracts.schema.json $defs/gate_record required = ['schema_id','gate_id','provider','repository_binding_ref','provider_review_id','source','provider_gate_identity','enforcement','raw_status','normalized_status','binding_kind','binding','evidence_refs','observed_at_utc'] and names none of the three; its only two branches that name them, allOf[3] and allOf[4], are both gated on required:['canonical_url']. Validated with jsonschema: the fixture azure_policy_evaluation_gate_is_review_bound_to_the_merge_triple with canonical_url, canonical_url_origin and url_absent_reason deleted validates, while the authored negative (url_absent_reason set to null) is correctly rejected. No fixture exercises omission.
suggested_repair: Add canonical_url, canonical_url_origin and url_absent_reason to gate_record's required list and add a negative fixture that omits them.

claim: SCS-016's canonical_text gains the parenthetical '(the Source Location's own Host)', a semantic claim that no correction or card answer in this ledger asks for, in a unit the ledger's own AZ-19 record calls 'the minimal touch to a document another branch is also editing'.
evidence: Base text: 'Local filesystem work executes in the Source Location's authorized Environment through the selected installation'. Branch text: 'Local filesystem work executes in the Source Location's authorized Environment (the Source Location's own Host) through the selected installation'. No atom in records/design_atoms.jsonl names Environment, Host or their relation; atom-azure-az-19's obligation is canonical_url_origin and url_absent_reason only. The edit is not token hygiene either: 'Host' already occurs three times in the base SCS-016 block and is not in the unit's preserved_exact_tokens. The two other incidental edits in the same unit, 'raw and normalized status' to 'raw_status and normalized_status' and 'compact typed available actions' to 'compact typed available-action summaries', are token-hygiene repairs for registry entries that occurred nowhere in the base unit text outside the registry line, so they are justified where this one is not.
suggested_repair: Revert the '(the Source Location's own Host)' parenthetical, or carry it on a branch that owns that claim.

claim: AZ-11's headline rule, that a staleness with no head change is not reported as stale_head_changed, is stated in FGI-004's acceptance criteria and negative constraints but is enforced by nothing. review_revision carries no branch pairing evidence_state with evidence_state_cause, and no negative fixture rejects the mismatch, so the exact false report the correction exists to stop still validates.
evidence: $defs/review_revision has exactly three allOf branches: evidence_state const current implies evidence_state_cause const not_stale; contents_complete true implies incomplete_reason_codes maxItems 0; contents_complete false implies minItems 1. No branch names stale_head_changed. Validated with jsonschema against the authored fixture azure_review_revision_target_move_stales_without_a_head_change: flipping evidence_state from revalidation_required to stale_head_changed while leaving evidence_state_cause as target_revision_moved validates, and so does the pairing stale_head_changed with policy_evidence_expired. The two authored review_revision negatives cover only the current-with-a-cause case and the complete-with-a-truncation case. This also falsifies the ledger's own claim in state/compile_queue.json that 'Three obligations have no validator surface and are recorded as open questions q-017, q-018 and q-019': q-017 is the second research pass, q-018 the join key and q-019 the Azure fixtures, and none of them is this one.
suggested_repair: Add an allOf branch requiring evidence_state_cause to be head_revision_changed or force_pushed when evidence_state is stale_head_changed, with a negative fixture, or record this obligation as a fourth unenforced one alongside q-017 to q-019.

claim: AZ-26 asked FGI-015's criterion to name the surface that carries each of the seven facts. The amended criterion names no surface per fact, and the canonical_text's collective answer cites a 'point-of-consent' surface that exists nowhere in canon, so an unmeetable criterion has been replaced by an unverifiable one.
evidence: New canonical_text: 'Issuer, allowed host, non-secret token owner, requested scopes, refresh and revoke, and the separate Git-versus-API roles are recorded by the trust, instance and point-of-consent surfaces those facts belong to'. New criterion: 'issuer, allowed host, non-secret token owner, requested scopes, refresh/revoke and the separate Git-versus-API roles are each identified by the named surface that carries them' - without naming which surface carries which. grep -ri 'point.of.consent' over Plans/ returns only this FGI-015 block, its preserved_exact_tokens line, the derived Plans/.plan_index/plan_units.jsonl and the ledger's own records; no schema definition, PlanUnit, fixture or document section of that name exists.
suggested_repair: Map each of the six remaining facts to a named, existing surface, and either introduce the point-of-consent surface as a real owner or replace the phrase with the surfaces that exist.

claim: All three concrete validation surfaces SCS-023 names are incapable of testing it. Two contract files carry no enforcement field, and the shard check it names never reads the document SCS-023 lives in.
evidence: SCS-023 validation_surfaces: Plans/source_control_contracts.schema.json, Plans/source_control_contract_fixtures.json, 'python3 scripts/pm-shard-plans.py --check --config Plans/sharding_config.json', 'future gate-list projection and accessibility fixtures'. grep -c enforcement over Plans/source_control_contracts.schema.json returns 0, and the branch adds no gate-list or enforcement shape to either file. Plans/sharding_config.json lists 99 sources and Plans/Source_Control_System.md is not among them (confirmed by the ledger validator's own error 'governance coverage targets missing from sharding_config sources'), and Plans/_shards/source_control_system does not exist, so the shard check the unit names never reads Source_Control_System.md. The amended Azure units ADO-003, ADO-005, ADO-006 and ADO-007 disclose exactly this absence in prose; SCS-023 does not.
suggested_repair: Drop the three surfaces that cannot test the unit, or add the same 'stated and not yet falsifiable by a fixture' disclosure the Azure units carry.

claim: F3-561 names two final-GUI contract files as validation surfaces for a gate list with source and enforcement columns. Neither file is touched by this branch and neither contains any of the unit's subject matter.

Both files are unchanged between 4f5eda0d18 and 7380013f04, and grep -ic over each returns 0 for 'enforcement', 0 for 'gate list' and 0 for 'current checks'.

claim: FGI-018, and identically FGI-019 and FGI-020, name the forge schema, the forge fixture pack and the contracts gate as validation surfaces for planning-only promises that those files deliberately do not contain, since the ledger's own authorization forbids adding the fields.
evidence: Each of the three units lists Plans/forge_integration_contracts.schema.json, Plans/forge_integration_contract_fixtures.json and 'python3 scripts/pm-new-contracts-verify.py' ahead of its future-fixtures entry. grep -oic over both files returns 0 for merge_strategy, 0 for vote, 0 for vote_value, 0 for required_reviewer and 0 for requeue; merge_strategy was 0 at base as well, so nothing was added. The units' own texts say the decisions admit no field, and the addendum preamble says the addendum 'does not ... admit typed schema variants', so the named surfaces cannot fail if the promises are broken.
suggested_repair: Remove the three present-tense surfaces from FGI-018, FGI-019 and FGI-020, leaving the future fixtures, and add the not-yet-falsifiable disclosure.

claim: Plans/ledgers/v2/ledger_registry.json is re-serialized with every object's keys sorted, rewriting the nine pre-existing ledger entries that belong to other threads. The change is semantically empty but turns a one-entry addition into a 185-line diff and guarantees a conflict with any concurrent registry write in a repository where many threads land at once.
evidence: Parsing both revisions: active_ledgers is unchanged; compiled_ledgers goes from 9 to 10 entries; the only added ledger_id is pldg-20260918-001-azure-devops-corrections; comparing every pre-existing entry with sort_keys gives zero semantic differences; list order is preserved; the only other change is updated_at_utc. The diff nonetheless rewrites each pre-existing entry, for example moving ledger_id, title, status, phase, created_at_utc order to alphabetical for pldg-20260908-002-terminal-workflow-findings and pldg-20260909-001-research-decision-review.
suggested_repair: Append the new entry and update updated_at_utc without reformatting the existing entries.

claim: The branch repairs a test that was already failing at the base commit for an unrelated reason, and the ledger records 'named_tests: pass' without disclosing it. The branch's own fixture-count update could not have made that test green on its own.
evidence: Running python3 -m unittest tests.test_pm_forge_provider_fixture_gate against a clean archive of 4f5eda0d18 fails: test_closed_manifest_enrolls_all_four_provider_packs_once, AssertionError: 31 != 30, because scripts/pm-new-contracts-verify.py already carried EXPECTED_CONTRACT_PAIR_COUNT 31 at base while the test asserted 30. The branch changes 30 to 31 and 26 to 27 in the same edit as the legitimate azure pack change from (2, 1) to (3, 5); scripts/ is untouched by the branch. At 7380013f04 all nine tests pass.
suggested_repair: State in the ledger's validation_state or the landing record that the named test was red at base for a prior thread's unregistered contract pair and that this branch also repaired that, so the pass is not read as a property of the base.

claim: The compile queue records ADO-005 as a compiled PlanUnit for the CD-01 answer, but the branch-policy deferral lands only in the Azure document's section 4 and section 7 prose, not in ADO-005's own unit body, whose canonical_text still promises Policies/Checks placement with no narrowing.

claim: The authorization shard and the ledger registry entry both state the wrong lane split for the twenty-six corrections. The true split is thirteen Azure-owned, twelve common-forge and one source-control, not twelve and thirteen.
evidence: source_shards/authorization.md: 'The twenty-six split twelve in the Azure owner or its own fixtures, thirteen in the common forge contracts, and one re-owned out of the Azure lane into Plans/Forge_Integrations.md.' Counting state/compile_queue.json items queue-001 to queue-026 by target_doc gives Plans/Azure_DevOps_Integration.md 13, Plans/Forge_Integrations.md 12, Plans/Source_Control_System.md 1; counting the 26 atom-azure-az-* atoms by owner_hints document gives the same 13 / 12 / 1. The re-owned item AZ-26 is inside the twelve.

claim: Downgraded from should_fix to note after reading reports/research-topic2-20260917/landing/README.md and verification.json. My original claim, that no obligation motivates the '(the Source Location's own Host)' parenthetical, is wrong: 'Source Location' was a genuine registry orphan at base and the bundle discloses the repair.
evidence: verification.json cross_branch_overlap says SCS-016 was 'amended minimally for the nullable canonical URL, the Check status vocabulary and four pre-existing registry orphans'. Recomputing the base block with the preserved_exact_tokens and negative_constraints lines stripped gives exactly four orphans: raw_status, normalized_status, 'Source Location' and 'compact typed available-action summaries'. 'Source Location' was an orphan because the base folded scalar wraps as 'in the Source\n  Location's authorized Environment', so the token never occurs contiguously. My earlier check missed this because I grepped the whole YAML block including the registry line.
suggested_repair: What remains is minor: the orphan could have been cured by reflowing the folded scalar rather than by adding a parenthetical that also asserts the authorized Environment is the Source Location's own Host. Prefer the reflow.

claim: Amended, severity unchanged. The bundle shows the split is a deliberate lane convention rather than an arithmetic slip, but the convention is stated nowhere in the ledger, and by the only measure reproducible from the ledger records the split is thirteen, twelve and one.
evidence: README.md explains 'TA-011 is a defect in the common schema ... and is counted inside the thirteen common-lane items. TA-042 is a defect in Plans/Forge_Integrations.md the owner document, and is the single re-owned item counted outside both lanes', and verification.json repeats lane_split 12/13/1. Counting the 26 queue items by target_doc, or the 26 atoms by owner_hints document, both give Azure 13, Forge 12, Source Control 1; TA-011 is AZ-14, whose target is FGI-003, so it is already inside the twelve and moving it does not produce thirteen. At least one Azure-target correction, most plausibly AZ-15, must be counted in the common lane for 12/13/1 to hold, and nothing says which.
